sources.title: Laura L. Gámez, Iximche’ como centro urbano (2016)
sources.note: Direct nine-page PDF. Printed 1129-1133: foundation 1463-1470, western confederation versus eastern Chajoma’, 1493 revolt, 1524 abandonment and resistance at least through 1535. Rejects a single unified Kaqchikel kingdom.

sources.title: George F. Guillemin, The Ancient Cakchiquel Capital of Iximche (1967)
sources.note: Direct excavator article. Use physical finds and architecture; political interpretation and conquest chronology follow newer Gámez. Great Palace, Temple 2, ballcourt Structure 8 and drainage paragraphs.

sources.title: Penn Libraries, Manuscrito cakchiquel, Ms. Coll. 700 Item 221
sources.note: Direct manuscript catalogue: probable surviving copy 1619-1650, 50 leaves, indigo ink, family and community records in manuscript pages 1-17. Brinton edition relation documented.

sources.title: The Annals of the Cakchiquels, edited and translated by Daniel G. Brinton (1885)
sources.note: Direct bilingual primary edition. Heading immediately before paragraph 155: Haok ki xoh pax pa tinamit vae. / How We went forth from the City. Original edition spelling preserved.

sources.title: Spurlock Museum, Contemporary Maya Weavings (2008)
sources.note: Direct exhibition text: three Kaqchikel po’t blouses, handwoven backstrap loom, town styles, consultant Magda Silvia Sotz Mux.

sources.title: Working with lay midwives to improve the detection of neonatal complications in rural Guatemala (2020)
sources.note: Full indexed primary research, interface modifications: pictograms and Kaqchikel audio; five midwives alpha testing, then fifteen beta testing. No unsupported mortality benefit asserted.

sources.title: Tulane Stone Center, Mayan Language Institute: Kaqchikel
sources.note: Direct program description: since 1987, expert local instructors, immersion, grammar, orthography and guest presentations. Mixed 2025/2026 schedule omitted.

sources.title: Mary W. Helms, Of Kings and Contexts (1986)
sources.note: Indexed original abstract and extended council-of-elders discussion read. Direct original PDF fails; institutional metadata also at digitalgreensboro.org/record/1008. Interprets decentralized authority, rather than treating kingdom label as settled constitutional fact.

sources.title: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, Miskito report (1983), Part One
sources.note: Full indexed original, A.7 treaty and 1894 annexation; later sections on 1982 displacement. Royal origin claims treated cautiously against Helms.

sources.title: Eleonore von Oertzen, Protestantism and Ethnic Identity (2005)
sources.note: Direct eight-page scholarly PDF, printed 45-52. Use historical trade/slaving, mission establishment and household conflict; do not adopt thesis that missions alone enabled ethnic survival or old population totals.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Canoe paddle model, 13/2491
sources.note: Direct institutional object record. Miskito attribution; carved wood model/miniature; collected by David E. Harrower in 1924 on Rio Coco, Sang Sang and San Carlos, Waspam. Collection date is not manufacture date.

sources.title: Eduard Conzemius, Ethnographical Survey of the Miskito and Sumu Indians (1932)
sources.note: Full indexed original printed page 67 turtle-spearing passage. Exact query site.repository.si.edu "Conzemius" "TURTLE SPEARING". Direct extraction failed. Paragraph uses specific Miskito terms, no transfer of Sumu-only customs.

sources.title: Indigenous Women, Climate Change and Forests, Miskito women’s interviews
sources.note: Full indexed original printed page 151, Santa Clara, Tasba Pain and Esperanza interviews, 2010 context. Direct fetch 403. Query site.wrd.unwomen.org "Santa Clara" "cassava" reproduces complete page.

sources.title: Ruby Morales Quant, Marcos Padilla Brown and Yuri Zapata Webb, La ortografía acentual en la lengua miskitu (2007)
sources.note: Direct 17-page PDF, printed 28-44. Printed 36/PDF index 8: wina (carne o cuerpo) versus winá (de o desde), accents as proposed by authors. Printed 32-33 field methods. Do not repeat erroneous introductory first-writing chronology.

sources.title: Nicaragua report to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, paragraphs 108-111
sources.note: Full indexed official state report, 2008-era document: 1987 statute, councils inaugurated May 4, 1990, 1993 language act. Source records legal provisions, not proof that all rights are implemented.

sources.title: UNICEF Nicaragua, Community protection information (2023)
sources.note: Direct landing page February 2023 and linked Spanish brochure, printed pages 3-5: family, friends, elders, health and religious leaders and women’s organizations. Miskito edition explicitly linked; its PDF extraction failed, so it is not used as the writing witness.
